Business: Concord Enviro is a leading player in the watrer treatment industry, currently using SAP ECC as their ERP system. With the impending sunset clause of SAP ECC and increasing gaps within their system, the company had planned to migrate to SAP S4 Hana. However, gaps in processes and people alignment led to the decision to continue with SAP ECC for the time being, optimizing and fixing issues to ensure a smooth transition until the sunset clause kicks in.
Problem:
Concord Enviro was facing significant gaps within their SAP ECC system, which impacted their business processes and operations.

The company was planning to migrate to SAP S4 Hana, but there was a need for a deeper understanding of existing issues and process gaps before proceeding.

Identifying inefficiencies in the system, aligning people and processes with system capabilities, and training employees were critical to improving the migration process and system efficiency.

The company required licensing optimization to reduce excess costs and ensure a more efficient system.
Solution:
Desktop Review: A thorough initial assessment of the existing SAP ECC system to identify gaps.

Business Understanding: Engaged with business owners through site visits to gain an in-depth understanding of operations and processes.

Gap Analysis: Conducted L1 and L2-level analysis of business processes to map out the "as-is" situation, identify gaps, and understand the root causes.

People and Process Alignment: Recognized that majority of the issues were not solely system-related but stemmed from people and process issues. Proposed comprehensive training programs for employees to ensure proper process adoption.

Data Cleaning & Master Data Management: Suggested implementing a robust data cleaning process to ensure that data quality is improved and ready for future migration.

License Optimization: Implemented strategies to optimize licenses, ensuring that Concord Enviro only paid for the necessary licenses, avoiding excess costs.

COA Mapping for Consolidation: Provided guidance on the automation of COA mapping to enable smooth multi-entity level consolidation.
Outcome:
Concord Enviro decided to continue with SAP ECC, optimizing it until the sunset clause is triggered, ensuring business continuity.

Management was happy with the proposed changes, as they addressed both system and people/process challenges, leading to a more efficient system.

Licensing costs were reduced significantly by eliminating unnecessary or excess licenses.

Data cleaning and master data management practices were put in place, leading to more accurate and reliable data.

The solution helped to ensure that the company was on track for smoother migration to S4 Hana when the time comes.

Posponed fixed migration cost of around 2 crores for around 2 years, till that helped the existing process and people to get matured to go to S4 Hanna

Business: The client is a pharmaceutical trading company that sources active and non-active pharmaceutical ingredients - both domestically and internationally - and resells them to clients, primarily international buyers. Their operating cycle involves receiving goods within a week and dispatching them in a shipment at the start of the following week.
Problem: The client was operating on Tally, which lacked the depth needed for their trading operations. Key gaps included the inability to track batch-level inventory, limited visibility into profitability by shipment or product line, no structured purchase order management, and no approval workflows. Reconciling purchases, receipts, and invoices (3-way matching) was cumbersome, and management had no consolidated view of pending payables and receivables.
Solution: Implemented Zoho Books and Zoho Inventory for the client. The engagement covered end-to-end system configuration including batch tracking for inventory, PO and invoice template creation as per client requirements, and approval workflows for POs, manual journals, and other transaction types. Bank feeds were also integrated directly into Zoho Books, pulling in transactions from the client's bank account automatically. Custom spreadsheet-based bulk upload tools were built for the item master and POs, complete with validation rules and usage instructions. Cutover data was uploaded to the new system to ensure continuity, followed by on-demand user support post go-live.
Outcome: The client gained batch-level inventory visibility, enabling traceability across their supply chain. They can now track profit per shipment and per product line (active vs. non-active ingredients). Open PO tracking and 3-way matching became significantly more streamlined. Management now has a real-time dashboard view of pending payables and receivables. Bulk upload templates reduced data entry effort and errors during both onboarding and ongoing operations. Bank reconciliation was simplified significantly - users can now match incoming and outgoing bank transactions directly against already-recorded entries, purchases, or sales within the system, eliminating the need for manual statement comparisons.
NewFiles:
Bulk upload spreadsheet for Item Master (with validation rules and instructions)
Bulk upload spreadsheet for Purchase Orders (with validation rules and instructions)
Custom PO template as per client's branding/requirements
Custom Invoice template as per client's requirements
FeedbackTeam: The client was challenging to manage on two fronts - timelines and expectations. While deliverables were largely submitted on time and the final output met the defined requirements, the client remained dissatisfied due to a perception that work was progressing slowly. Significant time and effort were invested in walking client teams through the system's features and functionalities, but the response was underwhelming - some teams were uncooperative, and none took a proactive approach to the implementation.
